text: dsh-agnes-image 是一个面向 DeepSeek Harness 的图像生成工具，通过注册 agnes_image 工具调用 Agnes Image 2.5 Flash。用户可以用文字描述生成图片，也可以提供一张参考图进行编辑，或提供多张参考图进行合成；可指定提示词、分辨率、宽高比和输出路径。生成结果以 PNG 保存到会话工作区，并返回文件路径及尺寸等信息，适合需要在 DSH 会话中制作或修改视觉素材的用户。使用前需要配置 Agnes API 密钥，插件会将提示词和参考图发送到 Agnes 图像服务。

dsh-agnes-image adds agnes_image to DeepSeek Harness for Agnes Image 2.5 Flash. Create images from prompts, edit with one reference, or combine several references. Choose resolution and aspect ratio; the PNG is saved in the session workspace and its path returned. An Agnes API key is required.
想直接在 DSH 对话里按文字描述生成一张图片。
能不能拿我提供的图片做参考，再生成修改后的版本？
I want to combine several reference images into one new composition from my DSH session.
dsh-agnes-image 的功能「文生图与图像编辑」：通过 agnes_image 工具提交提示词，可选提供一张或多张参考图，并设置尺寸和比例；生成的 PNG 写入会话工作区并返回文件路径。
dsh-agnes-image 的功能「选择图片输出位置」：调用工具时可指定相对会话工作区的 output_path；未指定时按提示词和时间生成文件名，并保存到 agnes-images 目录。
dsh-agnes-image 使用前须知：调用需要 Agnes API 密钥；插件按配置、凭据存储、环境变量和本地密钥文件顺序解析，未配置时会报错（见 lib/index.js:220-252）。
dsh-agnes-image 使用前须知：生成请求会把提示词及可选参考图片发送到 apihub.agnes-ai.com，并把返回图像写入本机会话工作区（见 lib/index.js:382-400、437-450）。

@dsh-external/dsh-agnes-image README · dsh-agnes-image：**One tool, three modes.** A [DeepSeek Harness](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@deepseek-ai/dsh) plugin that gives your agent [Agnes Image 2.5 Flash](https://www.agnes-ai.com/zh-Hans/docs/agnes-image-25-flash) (`agnes-image-2.5-flash`): **text-to-image**, **image-to-image**, and **multi-image composition** — with the result saved as a real PNG inside the session workspace, ready to show, present, or re-inspect with `read_image`.

@dsh-external/dsh-agnes-image README · dsh-agnes-image：Underneath the one-tool surface is the part most image plugins skip: **the network engineering that makes a lossy endpoint behave like a reliable one.** Everything in [Engineering deep-dive](#engineering-deep-dive) was measured, not guessed.

@dsh-external/dsh-agnes-image README · Why this plugin：| What you get | What it changes |
| --- | --- |
| **Three modes, one schema** | `image` omitted → text-to-image; one reference → image-to-image; several → multi-image composition. The model never has to pick a tool. |
| **Files, not URLs** | Bytes are requested inline (base64) and written into the session workspace. The agent gets a path it can render, diff, or feed back in as a reference. |
| **Deterministic connect path** | Pinned IPv4 on this plugin's sockets only — same request lands in **~9s instead of timing out at 20s+** (measured, see below). |
| **Loss-tolerant by design** | Bounded retry on connect-level failures only; HTTP statuses and aborts are never retried. |
| **Hot-rotating credentials** | API key resolved per call from 4 sources — rotate the key and the very next call picks it up, no restart. |
| **Zero runtime dependencies** | Only `node:https` + the harness SDK. Nothing else to install, nothing else to break. |
| **Readable failures** | Every error — including a message-less `AggregateError` — is normalized into one actionable line naming the attempt count. |

**API key resolution order** (re-resolved on every call, never cached): plugin config → harness credential store → environment (`AGONES_API_KEY` / `AGNES_API_KEY`) → key file. Key rotation reaches the very next call with no restart.

@dsh-external/dsh-agnes-image README · Engineering deep-dive：Four field-tested details are baked into ~470 lines of dependency-free code. Each one cost a real debugging session — the measurements below are why this plugin is reliable where a naive `fetch` wrapper is not.

@dsh-external/dsh-agnes-image README · 1. Pin IPv4 and disable happy-eyeballs — on our sockets only：The endpoint resolves to Cloudflare (`104.18.18.62` / `104.18.19.62`) **and advertises unroutable AAAA records**. Node's default `autoSelectFamily` runs a happy-eyeballs race: it burns the IPv6 attempts first and ends in a **20s+ all-address `ETIMEDOUT`**, surfaced as an `AggregateError` with an *empty message* — the model literally sees a bare `Error:`.
section: 1. Pin IPv4 and disable happy-eyeballs — on our sockets only

text:
@dsh-external/dsh-agnes-image README · 1. Pin IPv4 and disable happy-eyeballs — on our sockets only：The fix is `family: 4` + `autoSelectFamily: false`, collapsing the connect to **one deterministic IPv4 path without touching process-level DNS**:

| Approach | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Default (`autoSelectFamily` + AAAA) | Intermittent 20s+ all-address `ETIMEDOUT`, empty `AggregateError` |
| Custom `lookup` pinning family 4 | **Still reaches IPv6** (not honored on the multi-address path) — unreliable |
| `family: 4` + `autoSelectFamily: false` | **Stable success in ~9s** |
section: 1. Pin IPv4 and disable happy-eyeballs — on our sockets only

Pin IPv4 and disable happy-eyeballs — on our sockets only：> The middle row is the trap: pinning `family: 4` through a custom `lookup` still produced IPv6 addresses in the error — it is not applied on the `autoSelectFamily` path. Don't conclude from a single success.
section: 1. Pin IPv4 and disable happy-eyeballs — on our sockets only

text: @dsh-external/dsh-agnes-image README · 2. The route is genuinely lossy — retry, but only connect-level failures：An identical request can time out on every address one minute and answer normally the next. The plugin retries with bounded backoff (600/1200 ms, 3 attempts by default) and **only when no HTTP response was ever received**. `AbortError` and any HTTP status are never retried; every thrown failure is normalized into one line that names how many attempts were actually made.
section: 2. The route is genuinely lossy — retry, but only connect-level failures

text: @dsh-external/dsh-agnes-image README · 3. Fetch the image in one hop, not two (a deliberate trade-off)：The API returns an image **URL** by default, requiring a second network round-trip to a different host (`platform-outputs.agnes-ai.space`). In testing, generations *succeeded* and then **died on the download hop**, wasting the generation.
section: 3. Fetch the image in one hop, not two (a deliberate trade-off)

text:
@dsh-external/dsh-agnes-image README · 3. Fetch the image in one hop, not two (a deliberate trade-off)：So the plugin asks for the bytes **inline in the generation response**: `return_base64: true` for text-to-image, `extra_body.response_format: "b64_json"` for reference-image work. One request, one host, no download to strand. The URL path remains only as a fallback.

| Fetch strategy | Measured |
| --- | --- |
| URL + download (two hops) | 58.3s — and the download was aborted once mid-test |
| **Inline base64 (one hop)** | **16.6s** |
section: 3. Fetch the image in one hop, not two (a deliberate trade-off)

text: @dsh-external/dsh-agnes-image README · 4. `response_format` must never sit at the top level：The API requires it inside `extra_body` (same for `extra_body.image` on reference work). A top-level `response_format` — or `tags: ["img2img"]` for image-to-image — is silently wrong. The payload is constructed per mode accordingly.
section: 4. `response_format` must never sit at the top level

text: @dsh-external/dsh-agnes-image README · Known boundary: router-standard preset gating：The `router-standard` preset uses `tools.restrict` for progressive disclosure (whitelist = stage tools ∪ `META_TOOLS` ∩ `GLOBAL_SAFE`). `agnes_image` is not in that list, so under that preset it is **hidden in stages 0–2 and unlocked at stage 3** (verification/delivery). Built-in presets (`standard` / `minimal` / `ptc` / `cordis`) and no-preset sessions are unaffected.
